The algebraic-space valuative criterion has *unextended uniqueness* (at most one lift Spec(A)→X per valuation diagram) but *extension-allowing existence*: after possibly passing K'/K and to a valuation ring A' dominating A, a compatible map Spec(A')→X exists. The full criterion combines the two. This differs from the ordinary scheme criterion.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume $f$ is representable. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion
as in Definition \ref{definition-valuative-criterion},
\item given any commutative solid diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Spec(K) \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d] \\
\Spec(A) \ar[r] \ar@{-->}[ru] & Y
}
$$
where $A$ is a valuation ring with field of fractions $K$, there exists
a dotted arrow, i.e., $f$ satisfies the existence part of the valuative
criterion as in
Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-valuative-criterion}.
\end{enumerate}

The composition of two morphisms of algebraic spaces which satisfy the
(existence part of, resp.\ uniqueness part of) the valuative criterion
satisfies the (existence part of, resp.\ uniqueness part of) the valuative
criterion.
hypotheses: two morphisms of algebraic spaces which satisfy the (existence part of, resp.\ uniqueness part of) the valuative criterion
conclusions: The composition of two morphisms of algebraic spaces which satisfy the (existence part of, resp.\ uniqueness part of) the valuative criterion satisfies the (existence part of, resp.\ uniqueness part of) the valuative criterion.

reason: For uniqueness of a composite, apply uniqueness to the outer map and then the inner. For existence, use the outer morphism's valuative criterion to obtain K',A', a lift into Y, then apply the inner morphism to get K'',A'' and a lift into X; composition yields the required extension.
